headline: Your Perlego waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing higher-education institutions, colleges, and academic departments into the right Perlego unlimited digital-library, instructor-pilot, or affordability offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Gauthier Van Malderen.
productSummary: Perlego (perlego.com) is a subscription digital library for academic and professional books — edtech, not a per-title bookstore. Homepage: The digital library that powers your learning; We exist to make knowledge more accessible; working with educators and publishers to create a digital library of more than 1.5 million books, available anywhere in the world. Meta description on perlego.com: Save up to 90% on textbooks. Read over 1.5 million professional and academic ebooks in one simple space. Library logos: TRUSTED BY 5,000+ ACADEMIC PUBLISHERS (Cambridge, Taylor & Francis, Elsevier, Stanford, Wiley, Harvard). Product surfaces on the homepage: desktop-to-app reading (continue on phone or tablet); Smart Search as a research assistant that pinpoints relevant textbooks and passages; study guides created by Masters and PhD experts across subjects. Educators tab: affordable, high-quality course materials from 20+ disciplines and topics. Institutions tab: Join 200+ institutions using Perlego … online learning library of 1.5M+ books from leading higher education publishers. Pricing page (perlego.com/pricing): B2C Essential (800,000+ titles, Standard Read Aloud) vs Complete (1.5M+ books, Premium Read Aloud, Research Assistant); monthly, semester, or annual billing; worldwide; one-click citations; institutions & organisations copy Trusted by over 250 institutions worldwide; sales@perlego.com for bulk. Institutions page (perlego.com/institutions): partners with universities and colleges for unlimited access; no limits or restrictions when reading; faculty freedom to teach from any number of books; students go beyond the reading list; notes, highlights, AI search, Read Aloud; Subscription Manager for users and engagement; no concurrency or credit limits; OVER 100,000 STUDENTS; Trusted by over 450 institutions worldwide. Named institutional quotes: David Claivaz, Dean, Business School Lausanne; Melanie Bruce, Digital Learning Manager, Cambridge School of Visual and Performing Arts. Institutional pricing: price per subscription; up to 50 subscriptions annual fee per seat for 1M+ titles; 50+ volume/sliding scale; three plans by volume covering support, features, integrations. 50+ subscriptions: integrations with major authentication, Library Discovery Systems, and LMS. SUPC (Southern Universities Purchasing Consortium) approved supplier. Catalogue note: professional and academic titles across 900+ topics; Wiley, Cengage, Harvard University Press named; Elsevier, Cengage Learning, Sage and Taylor & Francis not in the unlimited model and added case-by-case. Instructors page (perlego.com/instructors): Instructors Pilot Program; unlimited access to over 1 million academic books and textbooks; study features for active reading; assignment features and student progress insights; 20+ disciplines; OVER 100,000 STUDENTS; Trusted by over 180 institutions worldwide (older line vs institutions page). Publishers (perlego.com/marketing/publishers): Trusted by over 5000 publishers worldwide; usage-based publisher compensation; in 2023 redirected 24.2 million learners from piracy sites; 180 countries. HQ on homepage footer: Perlego Ltd, 1 Waterhouse Sq, 138 Holborn, London, EC1N 2ST. Headcount and TAM account counts are not published on perlego.com — omit them from heroStats.
coreInsight: Gauthier already sells an unlimited academic digital library so higher-ed students stop buying individual textbooks and institutions stop running course materials as per-title, concurrent-user, or credit-capped access. The one list is higher education only: universities, colleges, and academic departments that provision course materials or library access to learners — not multi-industry corporates, not a second publisher waterfall. The one routing signal is campus_course_materials_state: how the campus already puts textbooks in students' hands, because library/bookstore/LMS scrapes plus syllabus and affordability-page checks return a named inclusive-access or e-textbook competitor, a high-cost required reading list with no campus-wide unlimited library, a public textbook-affordability / WP / EDI page with no unlimited library named, or none of those, in one pull. Buyer title (librarian, faculty, student-success, procurement) is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how the campus already puts textbooks in students' hands
sections.takeaway: A library, bookstore, or LMS scrape plus syllabus and affordability-page checks already name an inclusive-access or e-textbook competitor, a high-cost required reading list with no unlimited library, or a public equity/affordability page with no Perlego-class catalogue. That course-materials state is stronger than a title guess, and it is cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM university, college, and department
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Named campus e-textbook / inclusive-access competitors go first, then departments with expensive required reading lists and no competitor platform, then institutions that publish textbook-affordability or WP pages without an unlimited library, then every remaining higher-ed account.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each course-materials state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Competitor inclusive-access stacks get a Campus Switch Brief. High-cost reading lists get an Instructor Pilot Brief. Affordability/WP pages with no unlimited library get an Access & Equity Brief. The rest get the Institutional Library Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the campus platform, pilot with faculty, close the affordability gap, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always in-TAM higher-ed — universities, colleges, academic departments — aimed at librarians, faculty, student-success, and procurement. Discipline and title are merge tags, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the course-materials state already on campus
sections.takeaway: Notice the competitor platform, the expensive required list, or the affordability page with no unlimited library, poke the student-cost or faculty-freedom pain that state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competitor campus-platform route first
sections.takeaway: Start where the institution already pays VitalSource, Kortext, BibliU, RedShelf, Follett Access, or a peer and still runs per-title or capped access. Prove reply density, then roll instructor-pilot reading-list accounts, affordability-page accounts, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Apollo plus LinkedIn plus higher-ed directories (and UK/EU university lists, IPEDS / College Navigator, library staff directories) are the TAM Gauthier already sells into: universities, colleges, and academic departments that provision course materials or library access — higher-ed / learners only, not multi-industry. TAM account count is not published on perlego.com; treat size as unknown and keep each launch tier ≥~1,500 contacts.

The same library / bookstore / LMS scrape plus syllabus ISBN check plus affordability-page detection returns campus_course_materials_state: a named inclusive-access or e-textbook competitor, a high-cost required reading list with no unlimited library, or a public textbook-affordability / WP / EDI page with no unlimited library named — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Perlego positioning: institutional unlimited access with no concurrency or credit limits and Subscription Manager (perlego.com/institutions); Instructors Pilot Program, assignment features, 20+ disciplines (perlego.com/instructors); Save up to 90% on textbooks and student access quotes on the homepage; Smart Search, study guides, and app reading as the soft remaining-TAM offer.

Buyer title and discipline labels are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Publisher outreach is a different buyer motion (perlego.com/marketing/publishers) — suppress it from this cascade, do not run it as a parallel TAM. Apollo is email last after the domain is routed, never the TAM spine alone.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_platform detected (VitalSource, Kortext, BibliU, RedShelf, Follett Inclusive Access, Pearson Inclusive Access, Cengage Unlimited campus program, Chegg eTextbooks, or another named inclusive-access / e-textbook platform on library, bookstore, or LMS pages)
routingRules.why: They already pay to put digital textbooks on campus but typically still run per-title, concurrent-user, or credit-capped access. Strongest intent for Perlego's core institutional offer: unlimited access with no concurrency or credit limits, Subscription Manager, faculty free to teach from any number of books (perlego.com/institutions).

routingRules.if: in_tam AND no Tier-1 competitor_platform AND reading_list_gap = high_cost_required_texts (syllabus or bookstore required list still selling individual textbooks)
routingRules.why: The department still sends students to buy individual titles. Maps to the Instructors Pilot Program (perlego.com/instructors).

routingRules.if: in_tam AND no Tier-1 competitor_platform AND no Tier-2 reading_list_gap AND affordability_page = textbook_affordability_or_wp_or_edi_page_with_no_unlimited_library_named
routingRules.why: The institution publicly cares about access and still has no unlimited digital library named. Homepage meta: Save up to 90% on textbooks.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (universities, colleges, academic departments). Softest CTA. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Campus e-textbook / inclusive-access competitor live
tiers.trigger: Library, bookstore, or LMS pages name VitalSource, Kortext, BibliU, RedShelf, Follett Inclusive Access, Pearson Inclusive Access, a Cengage Unlimited campus program, Chegg eTextbooks, or another inclusive-access / e-textbook platform
tiers.pain: They already budget for digital course materials but students and faculty still hit per-title, concurrent-user, or credit caps.
tiers.valueProp: Perlego institutional unlimited access: no concurrency or credit limits, Subscription Manager, faculty free to teach from any number of books (perlego.com/institutions). 1.5M+ books; Trusted by over 450 institutions; OVER 100,000 STUDENTS.
tiers.dataSource: Library / bookstore / LMS scrape + BuiltWith / script detection
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; not published on perlego.com — keep each tier ≥~1,500 contacts before launch

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: High-cost required reading list, no competitor platform
tiers.trigger: Syllabus or campus bookstore required-text list still sells individual textbooks AND no Tier-1 competitor_platform match
tiers.pain: Students on that module still buy print or single-title ebooks.
tiers.valueProp: Instructors Pilot Program (perlego.com/instructors): licences so a cohort gets a personal online library; assignment features; 20+ disciplines.
tiers.dataSource: Syllabus / reading-list / bookstore required-text scrape after in_tam gate

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Affordability / WP / EDI page, no unlimited library named
tiers.trigger: Textbook-affordability, OER, widening-participation, or EDI page is live AND no unlimited digital library is named AND no Tier-1 or Tier-2 match
tiers.pain: The institution already published that textbook cost and access are strategic, and students still lack an unlimited legal library.
tiers.valueProp: Institutions page: remove barriers to learning; Save up to 90% on textbooks (perlego.com meta).
tiers.dataSource: Affordability / OER / WP / EDI page scrape

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM higher-ed accounts
tiers.trigger: In-TAM university, college, or academic department with a library / faculty / student-success / procurement decision maker and no Tier 1-3 campus_course_materials_state
tiers.pain: Course materials still depend on what the library licenses title-by-title or what students can afford to buy.
tiers.valueProp: Soft Institutional Library Playbook: 1.5M+ professional and academic ebooks, Smart Search, study guides, app/offline reading.
tiers.dataSource: Apollo + LinkedIn company + title graph after in_tam gate
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; catch-all must cover remaining TAM

launchPlan: Confirm in_tam definition: universities, colleges, and academic departments that provision course materials or library access to learners. Multi-industry corporates and publisher acquisition targets are out of this TAM.
Pull Apollo / Sales Nav, then library/bookstore/LMS scrape for competitor_platform, syllabus scrape for reading_list_gap, and affordability/WP/EDI page scrape.
Launch Tier 1 only until reply density is clear. Do not launch a tier under ~1,500 contacts. Do not invent employee-count or TAM numbers.
Add Tier 2, then Tier 3, then catch-all.
Enrich emails via Apollo only after the account is routed.
